findings.title: Date override path skips busy-time check and allows double booking
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is inside it, the function returns `true` immediately at line 134. That bypasses the `busy.every(...)` check at the end of the function, so existing Cal bookings and calendar busy times are ignored whenever the user has a date override. A fixed host with a 9-12 override and an existing 10-11 booking will make the 10-11 slot appear available, allowing a round-robin booking to double-book them. The date override should only bypass the normal working-hours check; busy times still need to be evaluated.

findings.title: Slot end is computed from start time in working-hours check
findings.body: The working-hours check computes `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`, which is identical to `start`; it never computes the slot's end. It therefore only verifies that the slot starts before the end of a working-hour range, not that the whole slot fits. For example, a fixed host working 9-10 with a 60-minute event will accept a 9:30 slot even though it ends at 10:30. Use `slotEndTime` or `start + eventLength` for `end`.

findings.title: Working-hours `find` logic rejects split shifts and allows days with no availability
findings.body: The callback passed to `workingHours.find` returns `true` when the slot is outside a given working-hour range, and any truthy result causes the function to reject the slot. With split availability such as 9-12 and 13-17, a valid 9:30 slot is rejected because it is outside the 13-17 entry. Conversely, if `workingHours` has no entry for the slot's weekday, `find` returns `undefined` and the code falls through to the busy check, treating the slot as available. In round-robin filtering this can drop valid slots for split shifts while still allowing a host with no availability that day to be selected. The check should find a matching-day range that contains the slot and reject only when no such range exists.

findings.title: Zero-length date overrides are never detected because Dayjs objects are compared with `===`
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct Dayjs object instances, so it is always false. The intended branch for an override whose start and end are the same is therefore dead code. For an all-day-unavailable override represented by start===end, slots overlapping that point can fall through to `return true` at line 134 instead of being blocked. Use `.isSame(...)` for the comparison.

findings.title: Timezone offset conversion discards the day shift, placing overrides on the wrong invitee day for large offset gaps
findings.body: The new conversion computes override start/end as minute-of-day after adding the invitee/organizer offset. If that offset moves the override across midnight, the date part is lost. For example, an organizer in UTC+14 with an override at 23:00 on Jan 2 and an invitee in UTC-12 should see it at 21:00 on Jan 1, but the naive `override.start` still matches the Jan 2 invitee day in `activeOverrides`, while the computed time is 21:00 on Jan 2. The override is then applied 24 hours off. The converted override boundaries need to drive the day selection as well, not just the minute-of-day.

findings.title: No test covers the stated round-robin fixed-host date override fix
findings.body: The PR's primary stated fix is that date overrides for fixed hosts are honored in round-robin events, but the added test only varies the invitee timezone for a personal event. There is no scenario with `schedulingType: "ROUND_ROBIN"`, a fixed host with a date override, and a round-robin host, and no case where the fixed host also has an existing busy booking on the override day. As a result, the new `checkIfIsAvailable` logic that skips busy times and mishandles working hours is not exercised.
